bib.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Appendix E. Lagrange Multipliers (pp. 707-710)

question: How do you find stationary points of a function under equality and inequality constraints?

results.claim: Equality constraint g(x)=0: maximize by finding stationary point of L(x, lambda) = f(x) + lambda g(x) over x and lambda; this gives D+1 equations for a D-dimensional x.
results.quote:
For a D-dimensional vector x, this
gives D +1 equations that determine both the stationary point x⋆and the value of λ.

results.claim: Worked example: maximizing f = 1 - x1^2 - x2^2 subject to x1 + x2 - 1 = 0 gives (x1*, x2*) = (1/2, 1/2) and lambda = 1.
results.quote: the corresponding value for the Lagrange multiplier is λ = 1.
results.note: Check: from -2x1+lambda=0, x1=x2=lambda/2, constraint gives lambda=1. Consistent.

results.claim: Inequality constraint g(x) >= 0 (maximization) leads to KKT conditions: g(x) >= 0, lambda >= 0, lambda g(x) = 0.
results.quote:
These are known as the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions (Karush, 1939; Kuhn
and Tucker, 1951).

results.claim: To minimize f subject to g(x) >= 0, minimize L = f(x) - lambda g(x) with lambda >= 0.
results.quote:
then we minimize the Lagrangian function
L(x, λ) = f(x) −λg(x) with respect to x, again subject to λ ⩾0.

results.claim: Inactive constraint gives lambda=0 and grad f = 0; active constraint gives lambda>0 and grad f = -lambda grad g.
results.quote:
We therefore have
∇f(x) = −λ∇g(x) for some value of λ > 0.

results.claim: With multiple constraints g_j=0 and h_k>=0, optimize L = f + sum lambda_j g_j + sum mu_k h_k subject to mu_k >= 0 and mu_k h_k = 0.
results.quote: subject to µk ⩾0 and µkhk(x) = 0 for k = 1, . . . , K.

limits: Geometric motivation only; no proof of the KKT conditions or constraint qualifications; defers to Nocedal and Wright (1999).
Sign convention: maximization uses +lambda g, minimization uses -lambda g, with g >= 0 constraints.
practices: For a maximization with an inequality constraint g(x) >= 0, impose lambda >= 0 and complementary slackness lambda g(x) = 0 (p. 710).
Flip the sign of the multiplier term when minimizing (p. 710).

terms.definition: A parameter lambda used to find stationary points of a function subject to constraints
Active when the stationary point lies on the boundary g(x)=0; inactive when it lies where g(x)>0

figures.caption: A geometrical picture of the technique of Lagrange multipliers: maximize f(x) subject to g(x)=0.
figures.why: Shows grad f parallel to grad g at the optimum

figures.caption: Illustration of the problem of maximizing f(x) subject to the inequality constraint g(x) >= 0.

problems: Text layer says '∇f + λ∇g = 0 where λ ≠ 0' for the equality case, while the inequality case allows λ=0 for the inactive constraint; this is consistent, just a context shift.
